name: Varsin Yuzu-Ginger Bark
description: Irregular slabs of cocoa-analog bark embedded with candied yuzu peel and crystallized ginger, made in small batches by the Varsin Collective, a worker-owned candy operation running out of a Tier 2 industrial kitchen.
flavor_profile: Bittersweet cocoa-analog base, punchy yuzu citrus, and sharp crystallized ginger with a slight heat; snappy break, rough texture from irregular tempering
slogan: Made by hand. Sold by trust.
cultural_context: Varsin Collective has a cult following among Tier 2-3 consumers who distrust corponation candy; buying Varsin is considered a minor political act, and their products circulate through informal networks rather than retail shelves.
story_hooks: The Varsin Collective's kitchen is raided by a corponation legal team claiming IP infringement on their cocoa-analog formula — but someone tipped them off, and the betrayal is internal.
A Tier 4 food distributor offers Varsin a legitimate retail contract that would require them to scale up and lose worker-ownership structure — the collective fractures over the decision.
The candied yuzu peel in Varsin Bark comes from a rooftop garden in Tier 1 that is the last known source of a specific yuzu cultivar.
